title: Round of Applause
cast: The oldest one in the book — deliver it with a completely straight face

blocks.text: **Leader:** Let's give them a round of applause!
Everyone claps — while running a small circle on the spot.
Works exactly once per camp, on exactly one person. Spend it wisely.

title: Standing Ovation
cast: Best straight after Round of Applause, before anyone catches on

blocks.text: **Leader:** That deserves a standing ovation!
Everyone stands up and makes a big letter O with both arms.
A standing O. That is the whole joke, and it lands every time.

title: Big Hand
cast: No preparation, no props, no shame

blocks.text: **Leader:** Come on everyone — let's give them a big hand.
Everybody holds up one hand and slowly spreads their fingers as wide as they go.
Not a single clap. Hold the silence for a beat longer than feels comfortable.

title: Seal of Approval
cast: Arms straight, hands flat — flippers, not hands

blocks.text:
Straighten both arms in front of you, palms flat and facing each other.
Clap them together from the elbows, like a seal.
_Three good slaps._
Arf! Arf! Arf!
Tip the head back on the last one. Balancing an imaginary ball on your nose is optional but encouraged.

title: Watermelon
cast: Mime the slice big — it is a very large watermelon

blocks.text:
Hold up a slice of watermelon in both hands.
_Take an enormous bite, ear to ear._
_Chew, and look delighted about it._
Ptoo! Ptoo! Ptoo!
The seeds go towards the leaders. This is traditional and cannot be changed.

title: Lumberjack
cast: Needs a bit of room — check nobody is standing too close

blocks.text:
Everyone swings an axe at the same tree.
_Three big chops — hup, hup, hup._
TIMBERRRR!
Everyone leans slowly sideways and topples over. The slower the fall, the better it looks.

title: Microwave
cast: The smallest cheer in the book

blocks.text: Hold up one hand and wiggle your fingers — the tiniest wave you can manage.
Beeeeep.
A micro wave. Say nothing else; let them work it out.

Reach over your own shoulder and pat yourself firmly on the back.
_Twice, with feeling._
Well done, me!

title: Cheerio
cast: One finger and a thumb, that is it

blocks.text: Make a small circle with your finger and thumb and hold it up to one eye.
Cheeri-oooooo!

title: Two Thumbs Up
cast: For when there is no time for anything longer

blocks.text:
Both thumbs up, held high, with the biggest grin you can manage.
_Hold it for three full seconds without speaking._
The silence is the cheer. Anyone who talks has to do it again on their own.

title: Firecracker
cast: Starts as a whisper and ends as loudly as you dare

blocks.text:
Rub your palms together and start a fizzing sound, very quietly.
_Louder. Louder still. Up on your toes._
BANG!
Throw both hands in the air on the bang, then drift them down like falling sparks, fizzing as they go.

Rub your hands together and hiss, starting almost silently.
_Build it up — the snake is getting closer._
_Keep building until it is far too loud._
SSSSS — CLAP!
One clap, all together, and then complete silence. The silence is the best part.

title: Rocket Launch
cast: A countdown everyone can join, however late they notice

blocks.text:
**Leader:** Rocket ready? Count me down!
**Everyone:** Five — four — three — two — one —
WHOOOOOOSH!
Crouch low for the countdown and spring up on the whoosh, hands together over your head.

title: Sizzling Sausage
cast: One for after a camp cook-off

blocks.text:
Lay a sausage in the pan.
_Sssssss — turn it over._
_Sssssss — turn it again._
Ssss — POP! Beauty!
Everyone jumps on the pop. It is the fat spitting, and it always catches somebody out.

title: Kookaburra
cast: Best after dark, when the real ones answer back

blocks.text:
Tuck your hands under your arms for wings.
Start a low chuckle and let it climb into a full laugh.
Koo-koo-koo-ka-ka-KA-KA-KA!
Let it run one round longer than seems sensible. Round the bay, something usually joins in.

title: Aussie Cheer
cast: Leader calls, everyone answers — the loudest three seconds of the night

blocks.text:
**Leader:** Aussie! Aussie! Aussie!
**Everyone:** Oi! Oi! Oi!
**Leader:** Aussie!
**Everyone:** Oi!
**Leader:** Aussie!
**Everyone:** Oi!
Aussie! Aussie! Aussie! — Oi! Oi! Oi!
Save it for the very end, or nothing after it will sound like much.
